tea.title: The radiator in 6C
tea.question: What did Mrs. Kessler want that afternoon?

steps.hint: Go up to 6C. The radiator is your reason to be there.
The tea is laid on a tray. Lift the tray.

clue.title: A Photo Supplies order slip
clue.body: PHOTO SUPPLIES. THURS. 13 JUNE. MRS. K., 6C. THE DEED NEGATIVES, ALL OF THEM. ACROSS IT IN ANOTHER HAND: NOT FOR SALE. A.V.

dressing: Windows open, awnings down on the street side.
Flags laid out in the lobby for tomorrow.
Iced tea, not hot: the glasses sweat on the tray.
The radiators are cold and the player is there to bleed one anyway.

friday.title: Friday's errand
friday.question: What left 6C that evening, and for whom?

steps.hint: Cam Ortiz is still on his round. He is back after twenty to seven. Wait.
He is home now. Go to 4C.
His jersey is thrown down where he came in. Lift it.

clue.title: A leaf from Cam's route book
clue.body: FRI. 19 JUL., 6.40 P.M. 6C TO MR. EWALD. HOLD. FIRST RUN SAT. THE FLAP IS MARKED ACROSS IN HIS PENCIL.

dressing: Every window open, shades half drawn against the low sun.
Electric fans turning in the flats that have them.
The sky yellow in the west; awnings cranked in before the storm.
The ice card in a window turned to fifty pounds.

stairs.title: The stairs before light
stairs.question: What did the nurse write down?

steps.hint: Someone on the first floor has not slept. Go to 1D.
Teresa Vale's flask stands by her things. Lift it.
Her watch lies on a folded paper. Lift the watch.

clue.title: Teresa Vale's note
clue.body: 3.05 A.M. ADELA VOSS. REAR YARD. RIGHT HAND: SHREDS OF WHITE KID LEATHER UNDER THE NAILS. T.V.

dressing: Wet sills and puddles on the landings.
Lamps out where the lightning took the lights; one candle in 1D.
Windows shut in a hurry, curtains soaked.
The street washed clean and steaming.

notebook.title: The writer upstairs
notebook.question: What did Jonah Price hear, and what did he make up?

steps.hint: Jonah Price dates his books on their spines. Go to 6B.
On top of his case: draw the book marked 19 July off the stack.
Now his draft on the table. Lift it.
He threw the first attempt away. Lift the wastebasket.

clue.title: Jonah's struck page
clue.body: 19 JULY. STRUCK THROUGH: 'A DOOR, THEN HER VOICE, THEN THE DOOR.' BESIDE IT: NO. THAT IS LAST WEEK'S EPISODE. I HAVE HEARD THIS DOOR.

dressing: A fan on the writing table and paper weighted against it.
Shades drawn all day.
Bottles of soda water in a basin of ice.
Moths at the lamp.

button.title: The mending basket
button.question: Who came to the seamstress that morning?

steps.hint: Lena Ortiz writes every job down the morning it comes. Go to 2B.
A parcel is finished and waiting on top. Lift it away.
Her tape lies across the box. Lift the tape.
Now the notions box. Lift it.

clue.title: A leaf from Lena's button book
clue.body: 20 JULY. ONE PEARL. 6C, FOR A GLOVE. WRITTEN THAT MORNING.

dressing: First light, grey and cool for once.
Washing hung indoors because the yard is wet.
A milk bottle and the ice card on the sill.
Leaves and grit blown in under the door.

drain.title: The yard drain
drain.question: What did the storm wash down?

steps.hint: The work order is for this morning. Go down to the boiler room.
The yard drain's clean-out comes through the boiler room wall. Draw the plug.

clue.title: A scrap of white kid with a pearl button
clue.body: FROM THE YARD DRAIN, WED. 7 AUG. WHITE KID LEATHER, TORN. ONE PEARL BUTTON ON ITS SHANK.

dressing: The yard drain still silted from the July storm.
The boiler cold and its room the coolest in the house.
Flypaper in the basement passage.
Coal bin swept and empty.

drama.title: The twelfth record
drama.question: What was playing behind the wall?

steps.hint: Cal Dwyer and Juno Kells trade recordings on Saturdays at three. Go to 5B.
He files by ear. Lift the headphones off the stack first.
Top shelf, first box: the twelfth of July. Lift it out.
The box beside it is the nineteenth. Lift that out second.
Under where they stood is one with no label. Lift it.

clue.title: Cal's timing card for the two broadcasts
clue.body: WLBQ. 12 JULY AND 19 JULY. SAME DOOR, SAME TICK, SAME SECOND. THE 19TH WAS THE 12TH PLAYED AGAIN. C.D.

drama.occasion: the last Saturday but one of August
dressing: Wireless sets loud through open windows.
The first school notices on the lobby board.
A fan still running but the evenings drawing in.
Peaches in a bowl.

bench.title: Glass from the ash
bench.question: What did not burn?

steps.hint: Omar Bell raked the ash pit at eight. Give him time to carry it up to his bench.
Go to 3B.
He sorts before he cleans. Lift the parts crate down first.
Then the first tray.
Then the second tray. It is under that.

clue.title: A dark slide with Omar's bench tag
clue.body: GLASS, DARK SLIDE, A.V. 13, FROM ASH, 23 SEPT. THE PLATE IT HELD IS BROKEN ACROSS.

bench.occasion: two days after the first fire
dressing: Radiators knocking for the first time since spring.
Windows shut; storm sashes stacked in the hall, not yet hung.
Coal dust on the basement stairs.
Asters in a jar.

duplicate.title: The sleeve check
duplicate.question: What did Adela give Sacha Reed to keep?

steps.hint: The quarterly sleeve check is at a quarter to eight. Wait for it.
Go to 6A.
Sacha Reed checks the newest box first. Lift box C.
Then the oldest. Lift box A.
Then the one between. Lift box B.
The sleeve is on the light table under the loupe. Lift the loupe.

clue.title: The duplicate deed negative
clue.body: ON THE SLEEVE: FROM A.V., JUNE. DEED SCHEDULE. 'TOGETHER WITH THE REVERSION OF THE ADJOINING PARCEL', 1 AUGUST 1929.

duplicate.occasion: the week after Columbus Day, Hallowe'en coming
dressing: Cut paper pumpkins in the children's window on the second floor.
Steam heat on and the windows fogged.
Bunting from the Columbus Day parade folded on the lobby shelf.
Dark by half past five.

plate.title: Plate thirteen
plate.question: What is on the half that survived?

steps.hint: Sacha said Tuesday the twenty-ninth, in the evening. Let the bath warm.
Go to 6A.
The plate box first. Lift it to the bench.
The chemistry cans stand in front of the light box. Lift them clear.
Raise the light box lid.
Now the loupe.
The proof is drying under the other print. Lift that print away.

clue.title: The surviving half of plate 13
clue.body: A.V. 13. THE WET DECK. AN ARM AND SHOULDER AT THE NEAR EDGE. A PALE GLOVE. SACHA: I HAVE NOT REPAIRED THE REST INTO IT.

plate.occasion: the day the market broke, two days before Hallowe'en
dressing: Extras cried in the street all afternoon; the evening papers are gone from the stand.
A wireless on in every flat, all on the market report.
A jack-o'-lantern on the stoop that nobody has lit.
Coats on every hallstand and doors left ajar for news.

box.title: Mrs. Kessler's box
box.question: What did she keep?

steps.hint: Her sale day ends at three. Mr. Ewald calls at four. You have the hour between.
Go to 6C.
The glove tray stands on the cabinet. Lift it down.
The key is where a careful woman keeps one. Lift the hairpin tin.
The card index is in the way. Lift the front card.
The piece she is appraising stands on the box. Lift it off.
Now the ledger box.

clue.title: What was in Mrs. Kessler's box
clue.body: ADELA'S NOTE OF 6.10 P.M., 19 JULY: 'BEFORE THE TENANTS DO ON MONDAY.' THE RECORD OF 26 JUNE, THE LIGHTNING ITEM MARKED. AN AUGUST RENT RECEIPT IN THE ESTATE'S NAME.

dressing: Poppies and a flag in the lobby for Monday.
Election posters from Tuesday still up on the hoardings.
The sale room full of things brought in to sell since the market broke, and nobody buying.
Nadia's Armistice card unfinished in the shop window.

she_asked_first.line: She asked for the negatives in June and was refused. In July something left her flat sealed, an hour before dark.

the_glove.line: White kid under the nails, white kid in the drain, and a pearl button sewn back on for 6C the next morning.

the_evening_was_made.line: What the house heard from 6C that night was a record of the week before.

the_reason.line: The deed was the reason, and the plate was what had to go.

the_case.line: She kept the note that gave her the date. The case against Mae Kessler stands without a confession.

events.slip: The market broke on Tuesday. Management has cut the allowance to ten cents, and the tenants are counting theirs. Expect smaller tips until the year turns.
events.before: The ticker is running behind and nobody in the house will say why they keep looking at the paper.
